_anchors.canvas.w: 64, twice the control. This sample is the direction my bias pulls toward, and it is here to be knocked down by looking rather than by argument (BACKLOG).
_anchors.canvas.originX: canvas.w * 0.41: the hips sit back of centre because the chest, the arms and the head all reach forward of them
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h * 0.56, so a body that hangs below the hips still lands inside the frame
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 8, above the knob's declared 3-6 range on purpose: this is the sample that spends everything, so the round can see what spending buys
_anchors.frames.walk: 8, two per named phase, and a multiple of the gait's four phases so every key pose lands on a frame
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left, held identical across all four probe samples
_anchors.light.curve: 1.25. Dark fur has almost no ramp to spare above the middle, so the curve stays close to linear or the animal turns grey.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector
_anchors.outline.enabled: off. The idiom he singled out had no outer line, and this run keeps that look - the edge is carried by outline.rim instead, which is what the silhouette locks measure.
_anchors.outline.inner: on, even with the outer outline off: this sample drops the silhouette line but still needs the joints, which is the pairing a gradient idiom lives or dies on
_anchors.outline.rim: ON. Without it this idiom fails the edge-contrast lock at 0.058, which is where the same idiom failed before. The rim is what lets a no-outline sample keep a readable silhouette.
_anchors.outline.material: the hide ramp: this body has no ink, and the darkest hide tone is what the rim reaches for at the shadow edge
_anchors.body.scale: 1: these bodies are authored at 64 px directly rather than scaled up from the 48 px arthropod
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.10 turn on a 23 px arm: about 14 px of hand travel, which is the stride of a knuckle walker - long arms take long steps
_anchors.gait.lift: 2.2 px = chest height (2 * ry = 19) / 8.6, the eighth-of-the-body rule at this mass
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0.18. Fur is the one surface in this project where per-pixel noise is the material rather than dirt - it is what a coat looks like without drawing a single hair.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 75 ms. 8 frames x 75 = the shared 600 ms cycle every sample in this project walks at.
_anchors.playback.scale: 3, because 64 x 3 = 192 px on screen, the shared cell size
_anchors.light.z: the lamp sits slightly on the viewer's side. Backfilled when the depth solver arrived: at -1 every surface faces the light and the body flattens to one tone, at 0 the light grazes and the far half goes black. -0.35 puts the centre of a mass around two thirds up its ramp and still leaves the lit and shadow edges at the two ends.
_anchors.gait.depth: canvas.w / 8 = 8 px. Backfilled with the depth solver; no track in this sample uses the z channel, so it is inert here. It is the body's half-width rather than 0 so that it already means something the day a depth track is added.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 8 px, and it is measured rather than chosen: a sweep at 6, 10, 16 and 24 returns the same shadow area from 6 onward. Past a few pixels the ray has left the body and there is nothing more to block it. 8 keeps a small margin over the saturation point.
_anchors.shadow.bias: 0.25 px of depth, and its job changed. It used to guard against a surface shadowing itself, and it could not: acne scales with curvature, so a lone sphere of radius 18 self-shadowed 198 px and still self-shadowed at eight times the tolerance. That case is now settled by identity - a convex part cannot cast onto itself - so the bias only arbitrates a tie between two DIFFERENT parts whose surfaces meet at nearly the same depth. A quarter of a pixel is enough for that, and acne measures zero at every radius and every bias.
_anchors.shadow.strength: 1 ramp step. On a five-tone ramp that is a fifth of the whole range, which is a readable value drop with a hard edge - the shape the ink verdict of 15/08 selected. 0 disables the pass.
_anchors.fill.x: +0.5, opposite the key lamp on the horizontal. A fill placed on the same side as the key lifts the half that is already lit and does nothing for the half that needs it.
_anchors.fill.y: +0.7, from BELOW. This is bounce: light off the ground back up into the underside of a body. Every fill in painting and photography comes from lower than the key for that reason.
_anchors.fill.z: -0.2, barely on the viewer side. A fill that faces the viewer as hard as the key does flattens the form it exists to recover.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.15, and it is the measured edge rather than a taste. His ink verdict of 15/08 requires BOTH a wide value range and clustered tone regions, and this knob moves them in opposite directions. Swept at 0, 0.10, 0.13, 0.15, 0.17, 0.19 and 0.22: regions improve monotonically, and the tree loses 23% of its value range between 0.15 and 0.17 (0.654 down to 0.504). 0.15 is the largest weight that costs no range on either subject, and it still buys a 7% gain in region size.
